chunks: Al-Mudhaffar ibn Ja'far ibn Mudhaffar al-Alawi narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Mas'ood narrated to us, from his father, from Ubaydillah ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, who said: Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha' narrated to me, saying: I heard Ali ibn Musa al-Ridha (peace be upon him) say:

The ruling among the Children of Israel was that if someone stole something, he would become a slave to the owner. Joseph (peace be upon him) was with his aunt when he was young, and she loved him. There was a belt that Isaac (peace be upon him) had given to Jacob (peace be upon him), and it was with his sister (Jacob's wife). Jacob asked for Joseph to take him from his aunt, so she became sad about that and said, 'Leave him until I send him to you.' She took the belt, tied it around his middle under his clothes, and when Joseph came to his father, she arrived and said, 'The belt has been stolen.' They searched him and found it with him around his middle. Therefore, when Joseph's brothers said, 'If he steals, there was a brother of his who stole before him,' Joseph kept it secret in his heart and did not reveal it to them.
ai.seo_question: What was the punishment for theft in the time of the Children of Israel according to Imam al-Ridha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Ridha (peace be upon him) elucidates the concept of 'Sunnah' as a pre-existing customary law among the Children of Israel, where theft incurred enslavement, a precedent established during Joseph's youth when he was framed with his aunt's belt. This historical context explains why Joseph's brothers immediately accepted the penalty of enslavement for Benjamin when he was found with the king's cup, recognizing it as the established legal norm rather than a new decree. This narration highlights the Shia scholarly understanding of how prophetic actions and judgments were often grounded in the prevailing customs of their time to ensure legal clarity and acceptance.
